target_customer: Developers and enterprises adding real-time video avatars to AI agents (roleplay, recruiting, telehealth, customer support)
problem: AI agents are limited to text and voice; developers want lifelike, low latency avatars they can add with a few lines of code.
business_model: Usage-based API priced per minute (listed at $0.06 per minute) plus enterprise custom personas
product_category: Real-time interactive avatar models and API

founders.name: Parth Radia
founders.background_notes: YC page: five years at Ericsson founding and leading a 35 person team on voice and video synthesis foundation models; before that a research scientist at AT&T Labs on neural architectures for 3D telepresence.

founders.name: Kaahan Radia
founders.background_notes: YC page: five years at Zipline as a perception engineer building a camera based detect-and-avoid system for drones; published research at CVPR and JAMA.

competitors.name: Tavus
competitors.what: Conversational video interface and real-time avatars
competitors.funding_then: Reported $40M Series B in November 2025 and $18M Series A in March 2024 (third party teardown; Sacra conflicts)

competitors.name: Anam
competitors.funding_then: Reported $9M seed in July 2025 led by Redpoint (one profile)

competitors.name: Lemon Slice
competitors.what: Real-time interactive video avatars for AI agents
competitors.traction_then: Launched publicly with the seed round
competitors.funding_then: $10.5M seed led by Matrix Partners with Y Combinator, December 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Photorealistic avatars at about 180ms time to first byte and real-time frame rates need custom foundation models for video and voice synthesis, which is research-heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Model quality is the only moat and funded competitors such as Tavus, Anam and Lemon Slice ship similar APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Synthesia launched an interactive avatar API in July 2026 and Google's Gemini Live Avatar became generally available in September 2026, per a third party blog.

market_need_then: Developers building voice agents wanted a face for them, and several avatar API vendors raised seed to Series B rounds in 2025, indicating demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses keyframelabs.com (suffix); acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Wordmark; not further described by sources
identity.visual_style: Developer oriented with bracketed monospace style labels
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and forward looking, for example 'Bring AI to life'

branding.community_and_virality: Founders posted a Show HN style launch about emotional photoreal avatars at $0.06 per minute; scale of attention not verified.

brand_strength.rationale: Keyframe is a common animation term shared by other companies and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Keyframe Labs is a Spring 2026 company with a two person team and strong founder backgrounds in voice and video foundation models at Ericsson and perception at Zipline. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. The main risk is a crowded avatar API market where Tavus, Anam and Lemon Slice raised money in 2025 and Synthesia and Google entered in 2026.
notes: Round added: VCBacked lists a seed dated 2026-06 with no amount; this single database entry was not confirmed by a second search or any press. Rebel Fund appears in press only for other companies. Location varies by source.
